content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-webhook-driven-crypto-payment-fulfillment-explained-digital-18|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Courses pakistan

Stripe's decision not to support Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ethiopia, and dozens of other countries is not a technical limitation — it is a business decision driven by correspondent banking requirements, local regulatory compliance costs, and risk modeling. PayPal operates the same way. The practical result is that a creator in Lagos with a real product, a real audience, and a real income goal is blocked at the infrastructure level before any transaction ever occurs. Understanding this is the first step toward choosing a different architecture. The correct response is not finding a compliant workaround inside the conventional system. It is building on infrastructure that does not require banking partnerships, local regulatory agreements, or platform permission to operate. NOWPayments operates on blockchain rails that bypass every one of these constraints.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture behind selling courses without Stripe involves leveraging free and paid tools to create a fully operational online store. This includes using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage. Additionally, integrating NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification enables secure and efficient transactions.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This solution is specifically designed for digital creators in countries where Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are unavailable or severely restricted. These creators can include authors selling ebooks, educators offering courses, designers selling templates, and musicians selling beats, among others. The goal is to provide them with the tools and infrastructure necessary to successfully sell their digital products without being hindered by platform restrictions.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure empowers digital creators to operate independently of restricted platforms.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The components that make this infrastructure work together seamlessly include hosting services, backend logic tools, order storage solutions, and payment verification systems. For instance, Cloudflare Pages and Cloudflare Workers can be combined with Supabase and NOWPayments to create a robust and efficient commerce stack. This stack can be deployed quickly, with some solutions offering deployment in as little as 48 hours.

To deploy this infrastructure today, creators can start by selecting the components that best fit their needs. This might involve choosing between different hosting services, backend logic tools, and order storage solutions. Once the components are selected, creators can follow the documentation and guides provided to set up and configure their commerce stack. This process can be simplified by using pre-configured solutions like the Edge Commerce Stack, which offers a comprehensive and tested commerce infrastructure.

To deploy your sovereign commerce infrastructure, start by selecting your hosting service, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Next, choose your backend logic tool, like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. Then, set up your order storage solution, which could be Supabase or Google Sheets.
